html:
The Grand Duchy of Finland was Finland as a self-governing part of the Russian Empire, from 1809 to 1917. It is the direct forerunner of the modern state of Finland.

For six centuries Finland had been part of Sweden. Russia conquered it in the Finnish War of 1808 and 1809. At the Diet of Porvoo in 1809, Tsar Alexander I promised to keep its laws, its Lutheran church and the rights of its estates. Finland kept its own administration, and from 1860 its own currency. The capital moved to Helsinki in 1812.

The 19th century built a Finnish national identity. Elias Lönnrot published the Kalevala epic in 1835, and Finnish gained ground against Swedish. From 1899 the tsars tried to Russify the country, which caused fierce resistance. In 1906 Finland got a one-chamber parliament elected by all adults, and women won the vote. After the Russian Revolution, Finland declared independence on 6 December 1917.
sum: The Grand Duchy of Finland was Finland as a self-governing part of the Russian Empire, from 1809 to 1917. It is the direct forerunner of the modern state of Finland.
